method: Differential whole-source review against reviewed Windows GNU SSE2. Normalized all2265 instructions, resolved GNU numeric and MASM anonymous/named branch labels to instruction indices, inspected all six residual differences plus full directive inventory and labeled constant declarations. Equivalent instructions not independently serial-reread.
findings: Six residual instruction spellings replace GNU movq with MASM movd using64-bit general-register operands: two in hash-many tails packing flags/length, and two in each scalar compression entry packing counter and flags/length. Assembly acceptance and encoding require MASM/object validation; no truncation or compile failure claimed.

Remaining2259 instructions and all branch destinations coincide after numeric/label/whitespace normalization. Hash-many register preservation,528-byte frame and scalar120-byte frames retain the reviewed Windows GNU behavior.
Scalar blend temporary remains XMM14, avoiding unsaved XMM10 modification. Save/restore sequences match GNU.
PUBLIC and paired PROC/ENDP expose aliases for three entry points. Code alignment16 and read-only constants alignment64 replace GNU directives; no explicit FRAME/unwind annotations observed.

Named blend constants33/CC/3F/C0 contain matching complementary32-bit masks. CMP_MSB_MASK contains eight words compared with four in GNU; inspected128-bit consumers do not by themselves make extra storage a defect.
limits: No MASM build, x86/Windows run, object disassembly, sanitizer or throughput measurement. Upstream reference-only; pHash/ASAN deferred.
